items.title: Do Amazon’s Black Friday deals really save you money? A new report casts doubt.
items.content: Almost a third of Amazon Black Friday deals “provided no savings at all” in the last two years, a report says. The retailer is pushing back.

items.title: U.S. retail sales slow just ahead of the holiday shopping season. A hint of trouble? Nope.
items.content: Sales at U.S. retailers rose just slightly in October after two months of big increases, suggesting households took a small but temporary breather before the start of the holiday shopping season.

items.title: I’m in my 40s. Should I accept a lower pension in exchange for naming my husband or child as a beneficiary?
items.content: “If I die before my husband, he will receive a lifetime pension equal to 50%–66% of my monthly benefit.”

items.title: Now’s the perfect time for networking. Here’s how to send a cringe-free email.
items.content: Hiring for white-collar jobs usually dips in November and December, so try sending “cold emails” to your network instead.

items.title: Fund managers just slashed their tech bets at the fastest pace in two decades — and this is the tail risk keeping them up at night
items.content: Investors are shifting their overweight positioning away from megacap tech and getting less bearish on bonds. Yet they still maintain exceedingly low cash positions as global growth forecasts are bullish.
